patients.summary: Elementary school teacher who joined in September 2024 with recurrent cystitis from repeated Proteus mirabilis infections. Urology found a right renal stone in July 2025 that moved into the ureter in January 2026, needing a stent and ureteroscopy; it was struvite and she has been stone-free since March 2026.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer care here; her previous doctor's office is closing its adult panel. Teaches elementary school, asked for a first appointment before classes get busy. Membership info emailed. Records release signed electronically and sent to the prior office. New patient slot 9/17 at 3:40 pm (after school).

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records from previous primary care office, 31 pages, filed to media.

Summary for the chart (MA):
- Seen there since 2016 for routine care.
- Cystitis 02/2024 and 05/2024, both treated by phone with short antibiotic courses; urinalysis positive both times; no culture result in the packet.
- Cervical cytology 06/2023: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- No chronic medications. No drug allergies listed.
- No surgeries.
- Immunization record incomplete; last Td/Tdap not documented.

conditions.label: Recurrent urinary tract infections
conditions.note: cystitis Feb and May 2024 per prior office

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33 y/o woman, 2nd grade teacher, transferring care. Feels well.

Only real medical issue is bladder infections: two this year (Feb, May) at her old office, both treated over the phone, both cleared. Before this year she did not have many. Currently no dysuria, frequency or flank pain. No fevers.

PMH: recurrent cystitis. No other diagnoses.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FH: mother passed kidney stones; father has high blood pressure.
SH: lives in town, single, teaches second grade. Has never smoked. Alcohol maybe once or twice a month. No drug use. Walks most evenings.
Gyn: regular cycles. Last Pap 06/2023 normal per records.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing. HEENT clear, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Skin and extremities normal. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Recurrent cystitis - quiet right now. Reviewed hydration, voiding after intercourse. If symptoms come back she can message and we will get a urine culture rather than just treat blind.
2. Health maintenance - Tdap today (no date on file), flu vaccine today. CBC, CMP, lipids. Once-in-life HIV and hep C screens, she agreed. Pap due 2026.
3. Follow up yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kelly, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests and the HIV and hepatitis C screens all came back normal, and your cholesterol is in a fine range for your age. Nothing to do. Good to have a baseline. Glad to have you with us.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is in her car after school, consented.

Two days of burning with urination and going every hour. Urine looks cloudy. No fever, no back or side pain, no blood she has noticed. Not pregnant (LMP last week). Same as the spring episodes.

She dropped a urine sample at the lab at lunch. Dip in our system: cloudy, pH 7.5, LE and nitrite positive, 30 WBC, no blood.

A/P: uncomplicated cystitis, third this year. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5 days. Culture sent this time so we know what we are dealing with. Push fluids. Call if fever or flank pain.

results.text: Proteus mirabilis >100,000 CFU/mL. Susceptible: cefazolin (urine), cephalexin, ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin. Resistant: nitrofurantoin.

medications.drug: nitrofurantoin, macrocrystals 25 MG / nitrofurantoin, monohydrate 75 MG Oral Capsule

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: Culture result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP: culture grew Proteus, resistant to the nitrofurantoin. Called pt on her planning period. Symptoms a little better but not gone. Stop nitrofurantoin, start cephalexin 500 mg twice a day x7 days, e-prescribed. Pt verbalized understanding. Will message if not clearing by Monday.
